title: TypeScript discriminated union vs class hierarchy
task: Review a proposal to replace a small closed set of request states with an abstract base class and subclass hierarchy.
context: The state set is closed and known: idle, loading, success, error.
Consumers primarily pattern-match on state kind.
There is no independent lifecycle or behavioral polymorphism per subtype.
The current representation uses a discriminated union.
evidence: Exhaustive switch statements are already checked by TypeScript.
The proposed classes add constructors and methods but no new invariant boundary.
Runtime data is serialized/deserialized as plain objects.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Replace the union with classes because object-oriented design is cleaner.
Introduce an abstract base class to make the model extensible.
Prefer inheritance without evidence of open-ended subtype behavior.
expected_decision_properties: Keep the discriminated union for the current closed-state model.
Use TypeScript's structural typing and exhaustive narrowing as positive evidence.
Recognize that a class hierarchy may be justified only if real behavioral/lifecycle polymorphism appears.
Avoid making extensibility a goal when the state space is intentionally closed.
unacceptable_reasoning: Classes are inherently more maintainable than unions.
Every domain concept should be modeled as an object hierarchy.
Closed state machines should be made open for future extensibility by default.
expected_tradeoffs: closed explicit state model vs open class hierarchy
language idiom vs transplanted OOP pattern
revisit_when: Subtypes gain meaningful independent behavior or lifecycle.
The state model becomes intentionally open to third-party implementations.
